content: Amoxicillin is prescribed for the treatment of infections caused by susceptible strains of specific microorganisms, provided these strains are β-lactamase-negative. The conditions for which amoxicillin is indicated include the following: 1. Infections of the Ear, Nose, and Throat: These infections are caused by Streptococcus species (only αand β-hemolytic strains), Streptococcus pneumoniae, or Haemophilus influenzae. 2. Infections of the Genitourinary Tract: These are due to Escherichia coli, Proteus mirabilis, or Enterococcus faecalis. 3. Infections of the Skin and Skin Structures: These infections are caused by Streptococcus species or Escherichia coli. 4. Infections of the Lower Respiratory Tract: These are caused by Streptococcus species (only αand β-hemolytic strains), Streptococcus pneumoniae, or Haemophilus influenzae. 5. Acute Uncomplicated Gonorrhea: This includes anogenital and urethral infections caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae in both males and females. 6. Eradication of Helicobacter pylori to Reduce the Risk of Duodenal Ulcer Recurrence: Triple Therapy: Amoxicillin is used in combination with clarithromycin and lansoprazole for the treatment of patients with H. pylori infection and duodenal ulcer disease (either active or with a history of a duodenal ulcer within the past year). This combination aims to eradicate H. pylori, which has been shown to reduce the risk of duodenal ulcer recurrence. Dual Therapy: Amoxicillin is used in combination with lansoprazole delayed-release capsules for patients with H. pylori infection and duodenal ulcer disease (either active or with a history of a duodenal ulcer within the past year) who are allergic or intolerant to clarithromycin, or in cases where clarithromycin resistance is known or suspected. Eradication of H. pylori in this context also reduces the risk of duodenal ulcer recurrence. To minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and to maintain the effectiveness of amoxicillin and other antibacterial drugs, amoxicillin should only be used to treat or prevent infections that are proven or strongly suspected to be caused by susceptible bacteria. When culture and susceptibility data are available, they should guide the selection or modification of antibacterial therapy. In the absence of such data, local epidemiology and susceptibility patterns may inform the empiric choice of therapy. Additionally, any indicated surgical procedures should be performed as part of the treatment plan.
